What it is

The biogeographical regions dataset is, in the words of its catalogue record, “the official delineations used in the Habitats Directive” and for the Emerald Network under the Bern Convention. The 2016 version (edition 01.00, 26 January 2016) corrected the Pannonian region of Serbia, among other fixes. It is licensed CC-BY 4.0 by the EEA and drawn at scales between 1:1,000,000 and 1:10,000,000.

The desk review listed it as a lead. It is in fact already in use: the pipeline reads it from the EEA’s map service, clips it to Kosovo in kosovo_biogeo_regions(), caches it as data/kosovo_biogeo_regions.gpkg, and uses it in the habitat screen, so that the crosswalk can differ between regions.

Kosovo coverage check

The pipeline’s cached extract answers the question directly.

Read from the EEA map service on 2026-09-29
Region Code Area in Kosovo (km²) Share
Continental Bio-geographical Region Continental 8,844 81.1 %
Alpine Bio-geographical Region Alpine 2,063 18.9 %

Kosovo is mapped; the regions carry no country attribute, so no country code applies. The line between the regions follows the dataset’s coarse scale and should not be read to the kilometre.

What it adds for Natura 2000 in Kosovo

Every Natura 2000 site is assessed in its biogeographical region, and sufficiency is judged region by region. Which region each part of Kosovo lies in therefore decides which biogeographical seminar would review its sites and which reference lists apply. The NBSAP names a clear delineation of these boundaries within Kosovo as a preparatory task; this dataset is the European starting point for it. It serves the national tier.

Caveats and sensitivity

  • Drawn at 1:1,000,000 or coarser: the boundary is good to about a kilometre at best, as R/functions.R notes.
  • No sensitive content.

Integration into the pipeline

Already integrated (kosovo_biogeo_regions() in R/functions.R). Nothing further is needed unless Kosovo defines its own finer delineation.

## What it is

The biogeographical regions dataset is, in the words of its catalogue record,
"the official delineations used in the Habitats Directive" and for the
Emerald Network under the Bern Convention. The 2016 version (edition 01.00,
26 January 2016) corrected the Pannonian region of Serbia, among other fixes.
It is licensed CC-BY 4.0 by the EEA and drawn at scales between 1:1,000,000
and 1:10,000,000.

The desk review listed it as a lead. It is in fact already in use: the
pipeline reads it from the EEA's map service, clips it to Kosovo in
`kosovo_biogeo_regions()`, caches it as `data/kosovo_biogeo_regions.gpkg`,
and uses it in the habitat screen, so that the crosswalk can differ between

## Kosovo coverage check

The pipeline's cached extract answers the question directly.

```{r}
#| label: check
#| eval: !expr file.exists(regions_path)
reg <- st_read(regions_path, quiet = TRUE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Region = reg$name, Code = reg$region,
                        `Area in Kosovo (km²)` = fmt_int(reg$area_km2),
                        Share = sprintf("%.1f %%", 100 * reg$area_km2 / sum(reg$area_km2)),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             align = "llrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("Read from the EEA map service on %s", reg$accessed[1]))
```

```{r}
#| label: map
#| eval: !expr file.exists(regions_path)
source("../R/functions.R", local = TRUE)
pal <- colorFactor(c("#009E73", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9"), domain = reg$region)
leaflet(st_transform(reg, 4326)) |>
  add_basemaps() |>
  addPolygons(fillColor = ~pal(region), fillOpacity = 0.4, weight = 1,
              color = ~pal(region), label = ~name) |>
  add_boundary_outline(kosovo_outline()) |>
  addLegend(pal = pal, values = ~region, title = "Biogeographical region") |>
  addLayersControl(baseGroups = basemap_groups,
                   options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = TRUE))
```

Kosovo is mapped; the regions carry no country attribute, so no country code
applies. The line between the regions follows the dataset's coarse scale and
should not be read to the kilometre.

Every Natura 2000 site is assessed in its biogeographical region, and
